title: Builder.io Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs, and Credits
summary: Builder.io pricing covers free and paid tiers, each with specific limits and features.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a free Builder.io plan, and what makes it not enough?


Because the free tier is metered in credits, it runs out when your publishing volume spends the allowance, not when your team grows. Each AI generation draws credits down.


Publish steadily and you will reach the end of the free allowance well before you need any paid feature. Check the credit allowance on the pricing page the day you decide, because the free figure has differed between older and current versions of the page.


### Does Builder.io charge per seat or per usage?


It does both, and the limit you reach first sets the bill. Paid plans carry a seat count and a credit allowance.


With heavy generation usage, a small team is limited by credits, so adding people changes little. A large team with light usage is limited by seats, so credits sit unused.


Work out your monthly generations and your headcount, then see which one forces the higher plan.


### Can I downgrade or cancel Builder.io mid-month?


Read the terms on the billing page before you commit, because they decide this and I haven't confirmed them. Two things matter.


First, whether a downgrade takes effect immediately or at the end of the billing period. Second, what happens to credits you have already paid for. If the answer is that they lapse, a mid-month cancellation saves you nothing for that month.


### Does Builder.io offer annual or startup discounts?


Annual billing is the usual way to lower the per-month rate, and the pricing page lists monthly and annual prices side by side.


The saving is real only if you are sure of your usage for the whole year, since you pay up front for a limit you may not need.


I haven't confirmed a startup programme, so ask Builder.io's sales team directly instead of assuming one exists.


### How often does Builder.io change its pricing?


Often enough that you should treat any figure, including those in this article, as dated.


Between older and current pages **the free credit allowance has already differed** , which shows the metered unit and its size can shift without the plan name changing.


Before you budget, recheck three things on the live pricing page: the credit allowance, what happens when credits reach zero, and whether unused credits roll over. Those answers decide the real monthly cost, and they are the ones that move.
